Theme

Common words: verbs, qualities & ideas

attitude noun

way of thinking and feeling about someone or something

also attitude towards, outlook, frame of mind, mentality, a good attitude, a bad attitude

classical

Cic. Fam. 13.77.1: hōc mē animō ergā tē esse
Cic. Fam. 3.9.1: quō animō inter nōs sumus
Traupman 153: bonō animō esse, to be in a good frame of mind

animus, animī m.

noun, second declension: with in or ergā and the accusative of the person

attitude, disposition, feeling (towards someone)

Latin asks “in what spirit” someone is: quō animō est in nōs?, what is his attitude to us? Bonō animō esse is to be in good heart (see positive). Animus is also the mind, courage, and intention, so the phrase around it decides (Lewis & Short).

Other words

  • voluntās, voluntātis f. — disposition, goodwill (towards someone)

    noun, third declension: with in or ergā and the accusative · also used · classical

    Will, wish; of feeling towards a person, goodwill or ill will, often with bona or mala (Lewis & Short).

  • mēns, mentis f. — mind, way of thinking, mentality

    noun, third declension · also used · classical · M-O s.v. attitude, mentality

    The mind as thinking; for a fixed way of thinking, Morgan–Owens gives it for “attitude, mentality”. The usual Latin for feeling towards someone is animus.

  • gestus, gestūs m. — posture, gesture

    noun, fourth declension · avoid · classical · Traupman 149, 274: gestus tuus mihi displicet, I don’t like your attitude

    Traupman’s “attitude” takes the English word in its old sense, the attitude of the body: classically gestus is a bearing, posture or gesture, as of an actor or an orator (Lewis & Short), not a way of thinking.

Examples

  • atque hoc ut tuī necessāriī sciant, hōc mē animō ergā tē esse, velim faciās eōs per litterās certiōrēs

    and so that your friends may know that this is my attitude towards you, please let them know by letterCic. Fam. 13.77.1

  • Bonō animō es: dūcēs uxōrem hanc. — Hem. — Bonō animō es, inquam.

    Cheer up: you’ll marry her. — What? — Cheer up, I said.Ter. Ad. 696

See also positive, be in a good mood, opinion.
